summary: Full backend + frontend E2E validation of new 'Desbloqueo de retiro parcial 40%' feature (LIONSBIT). Backend: 18/18 pytest cases green covering /partial-unlock/status, /start (idempotent), /proof (validation, FIFO priority, 404 when no pending), /support-request (notification fanout), /admin/queue (default in_review, sorting by priority_rank asc, counts, 403 on non-admin), /admin/{id}/approve (mirrors user.partial_withdraw_unlocked=true + max_eur snapshot, blocks already-approved with 400, 404 on unknown id), /admin/{id}/reject (empty note 400, status transition, 404 on unknown id). Frontend: complete user flow on /withdraw walked through — panel + 3 tiles + timeline + start CTA → payment-details (USDT TRC20 wallet, copy btn, €2660,00) → proof modal blocks <10 char hash and submits valid hash → in_review block with TX link + priority #1 → support modal opens, submits, closes → admin approves via /admin/partial-unlock (window.confirm) → user side flips to 'Aprobado · 40% desbloqueado' showing €30.194,00 unlocked + admin email + timestamp. Reject flow also verified: empty note keeps submit disabled, with note moves item to 'Rechazados' tab with admin note rendered. Sidebar 'Desbloqueos 40%' link present (1 in admin section). Regression on /withdraw hero card + tax info and on /admin/mt5-invest both intact.

issues: Amount shown as '€2660,00' instead of '€2.660,00' (no thousands separator). Spec text in panel header says '2.660 EUR' correctly, but the big amount tile in payment-details strips the dot. Cosmetic only — number is correct, just formatting inconsistency. Likely toLocaleString missing on that one node.

action_items: (Optional/cosmetic) Fix thousands separator in partial-unlock-amount-display so '€2660,00' renders as '€2.660,00' (use toLocaleString('es-ES',{style:'currency',currency:'EUR'}) or Intl.NumberFormat). Already correct in the 3 tiles (€75.485,00 / €30.194,00) and header text — only the big mono amount in payment-details panel is missing the dot.
critical_code_review_comments: routes/partial_unlock.py is clean, focused (~370 lines), correctly excludes _id via {'_id':0} projection, async/await throughout, proper HTTPException codes (400/404/403). Notification fanout wrapped in try/except so admin notif failure doesn't break user flow — good defensive pattern.

FIFO priority is computed as count(in_review)+1 at submit time. NOTE: this is not strictly stable if records are approved/rejected concurrently (priorities can be reused), but for this manual-validation flow it's acceptable and matches the user spec ('FIFO priority').

Snapshot policy correctly freezes available_balance + 40% cap at /start time (option 3a). Approve mirrors max_withdraw_eur_snapshot onto users.partial_withdraw_max_eur — verified via /partial-unlock/status returning is_approved=true after approve.
Admin endpoints all use Depends(get_admin_user) — verified 403 returned for non-admin user (test.bronce@test.com).
Admin reject correctly enforces note (400 on empty), but admin approve does NOT require a note (acceptable — note is optional metadata for audit trail).
PartialUnlockPanel.jsx + AdminPartialUnlockPage.jsx both expose all 20+ data-testid attributes the main agent advertised; testability is excellent.

Static demo USDT wallet address (TXwBxF3p5rz9dWwLsVyUvGJ2XhRyK8eQmP) is intentional per spec (human-in-the-loop validation, no on-chain check). MOCKED nature is correctly highlighted in the UI as 'Validación blockchain + firma admin' step.
No hardcoded URLs anywhere — frontend uses /lib/api which reads REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.
No PII leakage — admin queue returns user_email but only to admin role; queue endpoint is gated by get_admin_user.

success_rate.frontend: 100% (all flows: panel+tiles+timeline+start, payment-details+wallet+copy, proof modal validation+submit, in_review block+tx link+priority, support modal, admin queue+KPIs+filters+approve+reject, sidebar link, regression /withdraw hero+tax + /admin/mt5-invest)
